title: Interesting Update for Bloom Energy Stock Investors | BE Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate updates his Bloom Energy view with the cash-flow picture front and centre. Q3 free cash flow was negative $181m, which he explains as timing — booming sales mean cash goes out for materials and products before customers pay — plus deliberate investment in manufacturing capacity for demand he expects to last a decade or more; full-year cash flow is still positive at $42m and the company ended the quarter with $2.5bn of cash, so he sees no troubling situation. Management has raised guidance repeatedly, most recently in October: 2026 revenue is now expected at $4.5bn, up roughly 122% on 2025 versus a 60% growth forecast at the start of the year, and the operating margin guide rose to 22% from 14%. He quotes the CEO saying electricity demand will skyrocket for decades, driven by AI, EVs and driverless cars. On valuation, forward P/E of 38 looks relatively undervalued for triple-digit growth, but his DCF fair value is $156, leaving the stock roughly 20% overvalued on that metric — so overall he calls it fairly valued, is watching closely, and hopes to buy at a better price or on strong results at the same price. Call: BE HOLD reiterated (was HOLD 15 Nov, FV ~$155).

calls.base_case: Revenue guide $4.5bn for 2026 (+~122% vs 2025), operating margin guide raised to 22% (from 14%), $2.5bn cash and positive full-year free cash flow.
calls.bull_case: Electricity demand to skyrocket for decades on AI, EVs and driverless tech; data-centre power buildout keeps backlog and margins rising.
calls.bear_case: Q3 free cash flow was -$181m on working-capital timing; paying above his $156 DCF value leaves no margin of safety.
